identity.resolvedIdentity: Norderhov gamle prestegård, den historiske hovedbygningen som i dag huser Ringerikes Museum ved Norderhovsbakken 8.
identity.identityProblem: Prestegården, Ringerikes Museum, Norderhov kirke, Munkestua og det historiske gårdslandskapet er nært knyttet, men ikke samme fysiske objekt.
identity.splitReason: Prestegårdens hovedbygning og museet deler samme bygg. Kirken, Munkestua og det større gårdslandskapet håndteres som separate komponenter.

requiredEvidence: named museum point in the historic rectory

evidence.finding: Ringerikes Museum is named at 60.13189, 10.26845 in the old rectory complex.
evidence.reason: Direct named point for the institution occupying the historic building.

evidence.finding: Q11997890 identifies the museum building at approximately 60.13187, 10.26847 and gives Norderhovsbakken 8–10.
evidence.reason: Independent entity, coordinate and address control.

evidence.finding: The museum is located in Norderhov Rectory, used as the parish priest's residence from 1635 until the late 1950s, at Norderhovsbakken 8.
evidence.reason: Official current identity, building use and address.

evidence.sourceName: Buskerudmuseene – historical buildings at Ringerikes Museum
evidence.finding: Dendrochronology dates the ground floor of Svenskestua to 1635; the north wing followed in 1729, the south wing's second floor in 1745 and a new roof in 1822.
evidence.reason: Controls the surviving building layers and prevents treating 1716 as the building year.

evidence.finding: The museum interprets Anna Colbjørnsdatter and the Battle of Norderhov in 1716 in Svenskestua and offers guided access under museum conditions.
evidence.reason: Controls event association and present interpretation without proving every later narrative detail.

evidence.finding: The municipality describes the nearly 400-year-old timber rectory, the 1716 event memory and the first meeting of Asbjørnsen and Moe in 1826.
evidence.reason: Supports local historical layers and the separation from the neighbouring church.

evidence.finding: Independent geotagged images place the rectory and Munkestua at approximately 60.1317, 10.2689, close to the museum point.
The legacy coordinate is about 863.3 metres west-north-west of the rectory.
evidence.reason: Rejected because it does not identify the building or museum.

sourceObjectCandidates.rejectionReason: Matching independent entity control; OSM supplies the named operational museum point.
Represents Norderhov church, a separate active medieval church.
Does not identify the rectory and is more than 800 metres away.

rawEvidence.description: Persistent source control for the rectory building, 1635 chronology, 1716 memory, museum reuse, address and separation from Norderhov church.

decision.nextAction: Applied the named historic rectory and museum building as canonical, retained 1716 as the event year and separated the church, Munkestua and wider farm landscape. Continue with nore_stavkirke.

notes: The coordinate moves approximately 863 metres east-south-east.
The canonical point represents the historic rectory main building now used by Ringerikes Museum.
Year 1716 is an event and memory year, not the construction date of the whole building.
The Anna Colbjørnsdatter narrative must retain room for source criticism and later memory formation.
Norderhov church, Munkestua and the wider rectory property are separate components.
desc and popupDesc remain unchanged under place-description governance.
